heroHeadline: RSF and Arab Militias Massacre 28–97 Civilians in Misterei, West Darfur — Town Burned to the Ground
heroSubtitle: On Day 1139, RSF fighters and allied Arab militias launched a coordinated ground assault on Misterei, a predominantly Masalit town in West Darfur, killing between 28 and 97 civilians. Attackers arrived on motorcycles, horses, and armed pickup trucks from the west, flanking the town in multiple waves with assault rifles, RPGs, recoilless rifles, and vehicle-mounted machine guns. Satellite fire detection confirmed active fires over Misterei every day from May 29 through June 2; imagery showed extensive burn marks across all residential areas. Misterei is among at least seven West Darfur towns burned by RSF since April 2026, extending the pattern of ethnically targeted atrocities against Masalit and non-Arab communities documented since the El Geneina massacres of 2023. The attack occurred eight days after SAF formally derecognized the RSF as a state institution (May 18) and one week after the Treaty of Jeddah humanitarian framework was signed (May 20), demonstrating that formal diplomatic instruments have not halted RSF atrocities in Darfur. SAF continued drone strikes on RSF positions in North Kordofan on May 28 as the multi-front military campaign proceeds. Total displacement stands at 14 million+; 19.5 million face acute food insecurity as the June–August lean-season peak approaches; Chad's border closure following the May 25 Al-Tina market strike remains in effect, threatening the primary humanitarian corridor into Darfur.
